title: Assessing Quantum Layout Synthesis Tools via Known Optimal-SWAP Cost Benchmarks
problem: Quantum layout synthesis (QLS) tools insert SWAP gates to satisfy hardware connectivity constraints; existing SWAP-free benchmarks have known-optimal depths but do not evaluate SWAP count performance. Real-world applications require SWAP gates, leaving QLS tool quality assessment incomplete.
motivation: Quantifying SWAP optimality gaps is essential for evaluating QLS algorithm effectiveness and guiding future tool development.
method: Introduces QUBIKOS, a benchmark set with provably-optimal SWAP counts and non-trivial circuit structures. Evaluates leading QLS tools (LightSabre, ML-QLS, QMAP, tket) against known-optimal baselines, revealing large optimality gaps. Analysis of suboptimal cases provides insights for future algorithm design.
key_novelty: First benchmark set with provable-optimal SWAP counts enabling quantitative assessment of QLS tool optimality gaps.
contributions: QUBIKOS benchmark with provable-optimal SWAP counts and non-trivial circuit structures
Quantification of QLS tool optimality gaps: LightSabre (63x), ML-QLS (117x), QMAP (250x), tket (330x)
Analysis of suboptimal cases guiding future QLS algorithm development

metrics.other: SWAP count optimality gaps: LightSabre 63x, ML-QLS 117x, QMAP 250x, tket 330x
